properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 9:46PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Sunday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Sunday
morning and continue rising to 12.2 feet Sunday evening.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.2
feet on 11/24/1997.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon EDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 10 at 8:21PM CDT until September 11 at 2:15AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
FFWPAH

The National Weather Service in Paducah has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Ripley County in southeastern Missouri...

* Until 215 AM CDT.

* At 821 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Doniphan, Naylor, Oxly, Budapest, Gatewood, Fairdealing, Handy and
Briar.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 10 at 9:03PM CDT until September 10 at 9:45PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
SVRLUB

The National Weather Service in Lubbock Texas has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Eastern Lamb County in northwestern Texas...

* Until 945 PM CDT.

* At 903 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles west of
Olton, moving southeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Olton, Fieldton, and Spade.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 10 at 7:00PM CDT until September 10 at 9:15PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
At 700 PM CDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain in Flooding reported in Lake Tanglewood. .
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall
rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to
2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lake Tanglewood and Palo Duro Canyon.

The Palo Duro Canyon Rim picked up about a half an inch in 10 minutes
and the floor recently picked up an inch in just 15 minutes.  Low
lying areas need to take caution as these rain rates could lead to
more significant flooding conditions in the Palo Duro Canyon area.
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 10 at 8:09PM EDT until September 11 at 12:15AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
At 809 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall
amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Jackson, Wellston, Hamden, Coalton, Wilkesville, Byer, Radcliffe
and Salem Center.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 2:57PM CDT until September 11 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 25.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 PM CDT Thursday was 25.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
evening and continue falling to 18.9 feet early Tuesday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 25.0
feet on 10/29/1975.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 10 at 8:33PM CDT until September 10 at 10:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 833 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated that showers and thunderstorms
were diminishing in intensity and coverage over the warned area.
Radar estimates that earlier heavy rainfall amounts between 1 and 2
inches with locally higher totals have likely fallen over portions of
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Pecos County, including portions of
U.S. Highway 285 southeast of Fort Stockton.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
